hooks.text: A single storm on Saturn can wrap around the entire planet.
Saturn looks peaceful, but one storm can swallow the entire planet.
Every thirty years, an Earth-sized storm wraps entirely around Saturn.

title: The Storm That Ate Its Own Tail
description: Saturn unleashes colossal megastorms so massive their tails wrap around the entire planet until they collide with their own head.

beats.text: A single storm on Saturn can wrap around the entire planet.
beats.visual: Cassini wide-angle view of Saturn's planet-encircling storm, 2011
queries: Saturn Great White Spot Cassini true color

beats.text: Jupiter is thought to lack planet-encircling storms, but Saturn periodically erupts with colossal Great White Spots.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope photograph of Jupiter's Great Red Spot, 2014

beats.text: Six of these megastorms have emerged since 1876, returning roughly every twenty to thirty years.
beats.visual: Historical portrait of astronomer Asaph Hall who observed the 1876 storm

beats.text: In late 2010, NASA's Cassini spacecraft watched a storm head grow to the size of Earth.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft image showing the Earth-sized storm head on Saturn, 2011

beats.text: The tempest generated up to ten lightning flashes per second while whipping out a massive tail.
beats.visual: False-color Cassini image of convective clouds and lightning regions on Saturn, 2011
queries: Cassini Saturn storm radio plasma discharge

beats.text: Within six months, that tail wrapped entirely around Saturn until it caught up with itself.
beats.visual: Cassini photograph showing the storm tail colliding with its head, 2011
queries: PIA14902 Saturn storm head meets tail
Saturn Great White Spot Cassini tail

beats.text: Caltech scientists discovered heavy water vapor suppresses atmospheric convection for decades until cooling overrides it.
beats.visual: Caltech planetary science building or conceptual atmospheric convection graphic, 2015

beats.text: Chemical remnants from these violent eruptions actually linger in Saturn's skies for centuries.
beats.visual: The Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array radio telescope dishes, 2015
queries: Very Large Array New Mexico antennas
Karl G Jansky Very Large Array panoramic

beats.text: Those deep atmospheric scars remain until Saturn unleashes its next planetary monster.
beats.visual: Cassini natural color mosaic of Saturn and its rings, 2016
